reason: Accretion releases heat, so combining it with the young Earth should begin the melting needed for differentiation.
expectation: The young Earth heats up and at least partly melts.

effect: Accretion produced a magma ocean, setting up the separation of metal from silicate.
reaction: The distinction between molten rock and the growing metal core is useful.
reason: Gravity should help dense metal sink through the molten Earth, advancing interior differentiation.
expectation: Metal separates downward toward Earth’s core.

effect: Gravity was not a compatible partner; the magma ocean can instead combine with metal grains or convection.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarifies the next step.
reason: Metal grains are the more direct choice for developing Earth's metal-rich interior.
expectation: Metal will join the molten Earth and contribute to its core.

alternatives.reason: Convection may also advance the magma ocean's evolution.

effect: The metal is now in droplets within the silicate melt, ready for separation.
reaction: The intermediate makes the differentiation process clearer.
reason: Gravity should pull the denser metal droplets downward through the silicate melt.
expectation: The metal sinks toward the growing core.

effect: Gravity caused the metal to sink and merge, advancing the separation of Earth's interior.
reaction: The result usefully notes that metal can reach the core by several pathways.
reason: I’ll check what the sinking metal can combine with to complete differentiation.
expectation: The inspection will reveal the next available step toward a differentiated interior.

alternatives.reason: This known-compatible pair may advance the other goal.

effect: The sinking metal joined the magma ocean automatically, completing the differentiated-interior goal.
reaction: The distinction between ongoing separation and inserting a ready-made core is useful.
reason: The earlier compatibility report showed that convection works with the magma ocean; it may advance the crust goal.
expectation: Convection will change the molten silicate and move the planet toward forming crustal rafts.

effect: Convection brought hot melt to the surface, where it can lose heat by radiation.
reaction: The link between convection and surface cooling makes the next step clear.
reason: Radiation can carry heat away from the exposed melt, potentially allowing crust to form.
expectation: The surface melt cools and begins to solidify.

effect: Radiative cooling produced crystals in a surface layer, beginning solid crust formation.
reaction: The contrast between the solid layer and moving rock beneath it is clear.
reason: I’ll check how the crystals can develop into the crustal rafts required by the remaining goal.

choice.inspect: Crystals in a cooling surface layer

expectation: The inspection will reveal a compatible next step toward crustal rafts.

effect: The inspection automatically combined the crystals with surface melt, forming fragile crustal rafts and completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The temporary nature of the early crust was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following metal droplets as they sank and merged was most worthwhile: it made differentiation a physical process rather than simply adding a finished core.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first attempt to apply gravity directly to the magma ocean was unsuccessful; it added a detour before the required metal-droplet intermediate became clear.

surprise.text: I expected gravity to work directly on the magma ocean, but the game required metal droplets first.

arbitrary.text: Combining the crystals with hot surface melt to make crustal rafts was not obvious to me beforehand, so I relied on inspection.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how this temporary crust develops, since the chapter connected the combinations to physical processes in a useful way.
